title: streaming lifecycle: client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume and server timeout mapping (OpenAI compat)
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: production streaming endpoints need robust lifecycle controls for real-world clients. This PR standardizes client-cancel semantics, improves disconnect handling, and implements reconnect/resume paths with server-side timeout mapping. It also updates the OpenAI compatibility layer so reconnect/resume behavior matches common OpenAI client expectations.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced LifecycleControl protocol messages to the streaming runtime (Cancel, Disconnect, ResumeRequest, ResumeAck) and handlers in the server runtime.
- Implemented client-initiated cancel that immediately stops token generation and returns a terminal event; ensures KV-cache state is cleaned for subsequent resumes.
- Added disconnect detection and a short grace period on the server (configurable via STREAM_GRACE_PERIOD_MS) before marking a stream as timed out; this prevents premature server-side model state eviction for flaky networks.
- Reconnect/Resume: client can reconnect with a ResumeRequest containing last_ack_token_index and an optional session_id. Server validates and replays cached KV-context when available; when replay is not possible we fall back to a restart with a clear OpenAI-compatible resume-failure event.
- Server timeout mapping: unify internal timeouts with OpenAI-compat error codes and events so SDKs can react consistently.
- OpenAI compatibility layer: add hooks so existing clients get the expected sequence of events on cancel/disconnect/resume (e.g., `event: done` vs `event: error` semantics).
- Added end-to-end tests and SDK hooks in the TS/Python SDKs to exercise reconnect/resume.

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Default behavior is backward-compatible: if a client does not use LifecycleControl messages, streams behave as before. Resume path requires the client to opt in via session_id.
- Config knobs (grace period, max resume window) are runtime flags so operators can tune to workload patterns.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for lifecycle handlers and timeout mapping.
- Integration test that simulates a network disconnect and performs a ResumeRequest to verify tokens resume correctly and no duplicate tokens are emitted.
- Manual load test showing <2% increase in p99 latency in worst-case resume scenarios (acceptable trade-off for reliability).

Release notes:
- Streaming: improved lifecycle controls (cancel/disconnect/reconnect/resume) and OpenAI-compat mappings. Non-breaking.

review_comments: Evan McCarthy: Can you clarify how we avoid duplicate tokens on partial replay? The spec should state behavior for overlap between client-ack index and server cache replay.

Priya Natarajan: Reply: Server accepts last_ack_token_index and trims replay to start after that index. If the server cache is missing the requested window we emit an OpenAI-compatible resume failure event and fall back to a full restart. Added comments and unit tests to cover the missing-cache scenario.
Luis Ortega: Please make the grace period config per-tenant (not global) — this is important for Dedicated customers with high churn.
Priya Natarajan: Reply: Changed STREAM_GRACE_PERIOD_MS to be evaluated from tenant runtime config with a cluster-level default. Updated config/flags and tests.
Maya Chen: CI flaked on an integration asserting metrics; re-run CI after fix to metric name (streaming_disconnect_count -> streaming_disconnects_total).
Priya Natarajan: Reply: Fixed metric name and added migration note. CI rerun passed.
